significance: An open-air shrine north of Kathmandu whose five-metre black basalt Vishnu lies on a coiled serpent in a 13-metre recessed pool. The image is over 1,400 years old, is venerated by Buddhists as well as Hindus, and is protected under Nepal's ancient monuments act.
story: The stone is said to have been struck by a farmer's plough and unearthed by chance; King Pratap Malla's vision that a monarch who looked on it would die early has kept Nepal's kings away ever since.
